service.description: How Superset is reached from outside the cluster

nginx.description: nginx Ingress for the Superset web UI. Created only when host is set

host.description: Hostname to serve Superset on, e.g. superset.example.com. Leave empty and no Ingress is created (reach the UI by port-forwarding the Service on 8088 instead)

tlshost.description: Hostname to put in the TLS certificate. Defaults to the host above; set it only when the certificate is issued for a different name

tlsSecretname.description: Name of an existing Kubernetes TLS secret holding the certificate for that host

image.description: Superset container image, shared by the web node, the Celery worker/beat/flower pods and the init Job

repository.description: Image repository for Superset. Change it to pull from a private mirror. Must not be empty

tag.description: Superset version to run, e.g. 4.1.1. Raising this upgrades Superset; the init Job runs the database migrations on the next install/upgrade. Must not be empty - it falls back to appVersion "1.0", which is not a published tag

init.description: One-off setup Job: database migrations, roles, and the first admin user

createAdmin.description: Create the first admin account on install. Turn off once the account exists, or if you log in through an external identity provider

username.description: Login name for the first admin account

password.description: Password for the first admin account. The default is literally "admin" - change it before exposing Superset

email.description: Email address for the first admin account

firstname.description: First name shown in the Superset UI for the admin account

lastname.description: Last name shown in the Superset UI for the admin account

replicaCount.description: Number of Celery worker pods. Workers run scheduled reports, alerts and long SQL Lab queries, so raise this when charts queue up

enabled.description: Run the Celery beat scheduler. Required for scheduled reports and alerts to actually fire; keep exactly one of these
Run Flower, a web dashboard on port 5555 for inspecting the Celery queue. Useful for debugging stuck reports

resources.description: CPU/memory applied to every Superset pod (web, worker, beat, flower, init Job)

cpu.description: CPU reserved for each Superset pod, e.g. 250m

memory.description: Memory reserved for each Superset pod, e.g. 512Mi

limits.description: Hard CPU/memory ceiling per Superset pod

cpu.description: CPU ceiling for each Superset pod, e.g. 1000m

memory.description: Memory ceiling for each Superset pod. Below roughly 1Gi the web pod is OOM-killed while booting, because it pip-installs its database drivers before gunicorn starts

replicaCount.description: Number of Superset web pods. The web tier holds no local state (metadata is in PostgreSQL, cache and celery in Redis), so this is safe to raise for more concurrent users. With autoscaling enabled this is the autoscaler's minimum, since the autoscaler owns the replica count

autoscaling.description: Horizontal autoscaling for the Superset web pods

enabled.description: Autoscale the web tier. When on, the autoscaler owns the replica count and supersetNode.replicaCount becomes its minimum; when off, the pod count is exactly supersetNode.replicaCount

maxReplicas.description: Upper bound on web pods when autoscaling is on. Must be at least supersetNode.replicaCount: a lower value renders an autoscaler the API server rejects with "spec.maxReplicas: Invalid value: must be greater than or equal to minReplicas", which fails the upgrade

targetCPUUtilizationPercentage.description: Scale up once average CPU exceeds this percentage of the CPU request

targetMemoryUtilizationPercentage.description: Scale up once average memory exceeds this percentage of the memory request. Superset's web memory sits in the hundreds of MiB even when idle, so raise this (or the memory request) if the tier scales up with no traffic

secretKey.description: Flask SECRET_KEY. Leave empty and the chart generates one on install and reuses it on every upgrade. It signs login sessions AND encrypts the database passwords Superset stores, so changing it logs everyone out and makes saved database connections unreadable

featureFlags.description: Superset feature flags, as FLAG_NAME: true, e.g. {"ALERT_REPORTS": true, "DASHBOARD_RBAC": true}. Values must be booleans

config.description: Extra settings written into superset_config.py, as SETTING: value, e.g. {"ROW_LIMIT": 5000, "SUPERSET_WEBSERVER_TIMEOUT": 300}

connections.description: Database and Redis endpoints. Only used when the bundled postgres / redis subcharts are turned off - with them on, the chart wires these automatically

db_host.description: PostgreSQL host for Superset metadata. Always used, including with the bundled postgres - leave it at the default in that case, and point it at your own server when postgres.enabled is false

db_name.description: Name of the Superset metadata database

db_user.description: PostgreSQL user. Only read when the bundled postgres is turned off (with it on, the chart uses the credentials that subchart generates)

db_pass.description: PostgreSQL password. Only read when the bundled postgres is turned off

redis_host.description: Redis host. Always used, including with the bundled redis - leave it at the default in that case, and point it at your own server when redis.enabled is false. Supports Helm templating, e.g. {{ .Release.Name }}-redis-headless-service

redis_user.description: Redis username, if your Redis uses ACLs. Usually empty

redis_password.description: Redis password. Leave empty for an unauthenticated Redis

redis_cache_db.description: Redis database number used for the query/chart cache

redis_celery_db.description: Redis database number used for the Celery queue. Keep it different from the cache database

ssl_cert_reqs.description: How strictly the Redis server certificate is checked: CERT_NONE, CERT_OPTIONAL or CERT_REQUIRED

enabled.description: Deploy the bundled PostgreSQL for Superset metadata. Turn off to use your own database, then set the db_host / db_port / db_user / db_pass / db_name fields below

diskSize.description: Disk for the bundled PostgreSQL, e.g. 10Gi. Fixed at install time - a live volume cannot be resized afterwards

redis.description: Bundled Redis, used for the cache and as the Celery broker (zopdev/redis subchart)

enabled.description: Deploy the bundled Redis used for caching and the Celery queue. Turn off to use your own, then set the redis_host / redis_port / redis_password fields below

diskSize.description: Disk for the bundled Redis, e.g. 10Gi. Fixed at install time - a live volume cannot be resized afterwards
